title: Model collection: load a directory of scans, browse, keep/reject
description:
'A way to load all of the models in the collection and store that they are a collection before merging' and 'pick and choose between various of the generated outputs.' A collection is a directory of GLBs with *.settings.json sidecars (the Trellis2 settings in ~/crawfish: backend, resolution, steps, seed, decimation_target, texture_size). ModelCatalog.collection(Path) scans it; the membership and per-member keep/reject decisions persist as a collection.dsl manifest in that directory (one `load_mesh` per member, an `input_boolean` keep flag per member, members joined nowhere yet -- the merge is CRAW-16), honouring the one-language ruling. Scene side: a COLLECTION section in the model menu lists members with their settings summary, cycles the active member (keys [ ]), toggles keep/reject (K), and shows kept count; `ixdar-cli list-meshes` prints collections and members. ModelChoice gains Kind.COLLECTION so -Dixdar.model=~/crawfish opens the collection. Related: VIEW-6 (staging dir + sync-models), VIEW-7 and VIEW-8 (sidebar model switcher / click-to-load model list) -- the collection section lives in that sidebar.

Reopened 2026-09-06 (user review): (a) MemberMeshCache is a thin LRU wrapper, fold it into ModelCollection; (b) no hand-rolled JSON scanning; (c) the Class.forName desktop firewall in MeshLoader is not acceptable and glTF is not desktop-only: replace the Assimp-backed GltfMeshParser with a pure-Java GLB/glTF reader (header + JSON chunk + BIN chunk, accessors for POSITION/NORMAL/TEXCOORD_0/indices, embedded images as bytes) that compiles under TeaVM, and add a cross-platform JSON tree via Platform.parseJson (Gson on desktop/headless, browser JSON on web) used by both the glTF reader and the settings sidecar reader. Assimp stays only on the render-only AssimpModelImporter path.

Ruling 2026-09-06: texture UVs are per-corner, not per-vertex. The glTF loader welds exact duplicate positions on import (they exist only because glTF cannot express per-corner UVs) and stores the texture UV as a UvField implementation over the welded mesh, the same interface the seamless parameterization uses. The per-vertex _uv Vector3Field is replaced. IMG_4109 therefore loads as 468,350 vertices / 936,035 faces.

Ruling 2026-09-06 (second review): (1) texture UVs are NOT a bundle slot. They are a UvField (the existing pipeline interface) backed by a flat per-corner array, emitted by load_mesh on a `uv` output port of PortType.UV_FIELD, exactly like the seamless solver's output; TextureUv's slot constant goes away. (2) Thin data classes are out (new CLAUDE.md rule 'Avoid thin data classes'): GltfImage, GltfPrimitiveRange, GltfMaterial become parallel arrays on GltfModel; CollectionMember, ScanSettings, ScanSettingsReader fold into ModelCollection with the raw JsonValue kept per member; CornerSplitMesh is replaced by filling an ArrayMesh plus one float array.

Correction 2026-09-06 (discussion outcome, supersedes the port note above): the texture UV stays on the `_uv` bundle slot, whose value type becomes UvField. TextureUv is renamed to the generic array-backed implementation (CornerUvField: flat per-corner double[] u/v, implements UvField) because the seamless solver's output is the same per-corner data and will share the class (CRAW-28). No new slot name, no port.
definition-of-done: 1. -Dixdar.model=/home/acw/crawfish loads the collection, shows 10 members with settings summaries, and displays the first. 2. [ / ] cycle members without re-running any computation; K toggles keep and writes collection.dsl. 3. collection.dsl re-executes with ValidateDsl and reflects keep flags. 4. `ixdar-cli list-meshes` and uiState expose collection members and keep flags. 5. Loading a 40 MB member takes under 5 s after the first (cache the parsed ArrayMesh per member, bounded by a member count). 6. Build checkstyle-green.
testing-plan: 1. Unit: ModelCatalog.collection on a temp dir with two tiny .gltf + settings.json -> two members, settings parsed. 2. Unit: manifest writer/reader round trip of keep flags. 3. run-scene mesh-viewer --property ixdar.model=/home/acw/crawfish --keep-alive; `key ]` x3; `ui-state` shows member index; `key K`; check collection.dsl on disk.

The weld makes IMG_4109 non-manifold at 127 edges (24 already were before it), so HalfEdgeMeshEngine.buildFromIndexedMesh refuses the scan; CRAW-2 needs to decide whether the pipeline tolerates that or the weld must skip positions whose merge would raise an edge past two faces.

230 welded groups carry normals that disagree by more than 1e-3; the parser keeps the first source vertex's normal, so a glTF export (CRAW-20) that wants byte-identical shading has to split on normals as well as UVs.

The todo 'UvField on a load_mesh uv port instead of a slot' is obsolete: the correction paragraph in the description settles it the other way (the _uv bundle slot stays, no new port). Left in place rather than hand-edited out.
changes-made: ModelCatalog.collection(Path) + ModelCollection/CollectionMember/ScanSettings value classes: a directory of scans becomes a named collection, members named by file stem and sorted, *.settings.json sidecars read (never written)

CollectionManifest writes/reads collection.dsl beside the scans (staging fallback when the directory is read-only): one input_boolean keep flag per member then one load_mesh per member, both groups sorted, LF/UTF-8, so a rescan with no changes rewrites identical bytes
Manifest round-trips through PythonLexer/PythonParser without opening a mesh; keep flags keyed by the verbatim member name in name="keep:<member>"

SceneCollectionMenu: COLLECTION section in SceneModelMenu listing members with keep flag, vertex/triangle counts and the shared settings summary, clickable to load, plus prev/next/keep rows; MODELS list is suppressed while a collection is open
ModelScene gains openCollection/nextMember/prevMember/toggleKeepCurrentMember/noteMemberLoaded; MeshNodeViewerScene opens -Dixdar.model=<directory> as ModelChoice.Kind.COLLECTION and K toggles keep
MemberMeshCache: bounded LRU of parsed ArrayMesh per member (min(memberCount, 4)); revisiting a 40 MB scan measured 99 ms against ~10 s for the first parse
CollectionCommand terminal command (collection|cn list|next|prev|keep|reject); ui/state gains a collection block with members, keep flags, counts and settings

ixdar-cli gains collection-list/collection-keep/collection-reject and list-meshes prints collections with member keep flags; ixdar_automation_cli/collection_manifest.py renders bytes identical to the Java writer (verified against /home/acw/crawfish/collection.dsl)
MeshViewerKeyGuy now falls through to the scene's ControlHint bindings, which is what makes ESC open the model menu and ~ open the terminal in mesh-viewer at all
CollectionManifest/ScanSettingsReader read via Files.readAllBytes: TeaVM 0.15 cannot compile Files.readString, and ModelCatalog.collection is reachable from the web entry point
Launch entry 'CRAW-12: Mesh Viewer (crawfish collection)' in .vscode/launch.json; -Dixdar.model now accepts a directory

Rework: MemberMeshCache deleted; ModelCollection owns the bounded LRU itself (parsedMeshes map, meshCacheCapacity = min(memberCount, 4), loadMesh/cacheMesh/isMeshCached), and the eviction order is unit-tested with in-memory triangles rather than files

Platform.parseJson(String) returns a platform-neutral tree: ixdar/platform/json/JsonValue (public kind constant + string/number/boolean/items/members, get/getString/getDouble/getInt/getBoolean/isNull/asString), GsonJsonTree for LwjglPlatform and HeadlessPlatform, WebJsonTree over the browser's JSON.parse through TeaVM JSO for WebPlatform
ScanSettingsReader's hand-rolled scanner deleted; it now reads the sidecar through Platform.parseJson and keeps every scalar member as the document spelled it

GltfMeshParser rewritten as pure Java: GLB header + JSON chunk + BIN chunk read in place, .gltf with data: URI or external .bin, node/TRS/matrix transforms baked, accessors for POSITION/NORMAL/TEXCOORD_0 and 5121/5123/5125 indices with byteStride and byteOffset, triangles only (any other mode is an IOException naming it), bulk float/int copies from a little-endian ByteBuffer

MeshLoader.GLTF_PARSER_SIMPLE_NAME and the Class.forName packagePrefix firewall deleted; MeshLoader calls GltfMeshParser directly and glTF is no longer desktop-only. AssimpModelImporter (render path) untouched

GltfModel/GltfImage/GltfMaterial/GltfPrimitiveRange value classes expose the embedded images as bytes with their MIME type, each material's pbrMetallicRoughness factors and texture indices, the texture-to-image map and the per-primitive triangle ranges, so CRAW-3 can build a material slot without Assimp. GltfMeshParser.read() collects images; load() skips them

Weld ruling: the parser merges bitwise-identical positions (no epsilon) and TEXCOORD_0 now rides the bundle as ixdar/geometry/mesh/data/TextureUv, a per-corner UvField over a flat float[faceCount*3*2] owning its own SLOT constant. MeshLoader.UV_SLOT and the per-vertex _uv Vector3Field are gone

CornerUvSplit + CornerSplitMesh invert the weld for the renderer and the exporter, re-splitting a vertex once per distinct corner UV; round-trip tested on two_triangles.gltf (4 -> 4) and on a new two_triangles_seam.gltf fixture (6 source -> 4 welded -> 6 split)

IMG_4109 loads as 468,350 vertices / 936,035 faces (622,652 source vertices welded); boundary edges drop from 298,043 to 945 and non-manifold edges rise from 24 to 127; 230 welded groups disagreed on a normal by more than 1e-3, so an exporter wanting the file's original shading must split on normals too
Pure-Java parser beats Assimp on the 38 MB scan: cold 144.5ms vs 249.7ms, warm 52.8ms vs 124.9ms; peak heap 216 MiB vs 135 MiB, the difference being the 2,808,105-corner UV array

TeaVM output now contains GltfMeshParser, TextureUv, JsonValue and WebJsonTree and zero Gson or Assimp classes; ixdar_automation_cli/mesh_catalog notes that its accessor counts are the file's, not the welded loader's

Third pass: texture UVs stay on the existing _uv bundle slot; TextureUv renamed to CornerUvField (ixdar/geometry/mesh/data), the generic array-backed UvField over flat per-corner double[] cornerU/cornerV, owning SLOT = _uv. Nothing texture-specific in the name or docs, so CRAW-28's seamless output materializes into the same class; the _texture_uv name is gone everywhere

Applied the new 'Avoid thin data classes' rule: GltfImage, GltfMaterial and GltfPrimitiveRange deleted, their data now parallel arrays on GltfModel (imageBytes/imageMimeType/imageName, primitiveFaceStart/primitiveFaceCount/primitiveMaterial, materialName/baseColorFactor/emissiveFactor/metallicFactor/roughnessFactor and the five texture-index arrays, textureImage), filled by GltfMeshParser which is their only producer

CollectionMember, ScanSettings and ScanSettingsReader deleted; ModelCollection holds memberNames/memberPaths/memberSettings (the raw parsed JsonValue, null when absent)/memberKeep/memberVertexCount/memberTriangleCount, and ModelCollection.settingsSummary walks a sidecar's keys sorted. The menu, terminal command, ui-state and the Python CLI all print that same sorted summary
CornerSplitMesh deleted; CornerUvSplit.split(mesh, uv, splitUv) fills and returns an ArrayMesh with the split per-vertex UVs written into the caller-supplied float array, sized by maxSplitUvLength

Cursor and member APIs move to indices: ModelCollection.next/prev/select/selectPath/index return an int member index, ModelScene gains currentMemberIndex() and loadMember(int); the manifest writer sorts an index permutation so the bytes stay identical

Verified after the fold: 179 unit tests with only the known DenseMeshFewSplitsTest baseline failure, 30 Python CLI tests, TeaVM green with GltfMeshParser/GltfModel/CornerUvField/JsonValue/WebJsonTree present and zero Gson or TextureUv references, crawfish counts unchanged at 468350/936035, cached member reload 157 ms, manifest still byte-identical between the Java and Python writers
